rows.title: CT reserved $1,000 pandemic bonuses for 30,000 workers. At least 255,000 want them.
rows.standfirst: Demand for the Premium Pay Program far outweighs what the state budgeted, leading some lawmakers to call for increased funding.

rows.title: Housekeepers know they’re essential. They want to get treated like it.
rows.standfirst: Many housekeepers at Connecticut hospitals say COVID-19 pandemic benefits have only come after prolonged demands for recognition, if at all.

rows.title: CT gubernatorial campaigns struggle to be forthright on taxes
rows.standfirst: Bob Stefanowski says Gov. Ned Lamont “is a liar” about his record on cutting taxes, but some say Stefanowski wasn’t clear about his 2018 plan.

rows.title: Bob Stefanowski unveils $2 billion tax relief plan for CT
rows.standfirst: GOP gubernatorial candidate Bob Stefanowski’s plan would tap into CT’s rainy day fund to extend fuel tax relief and ease tax burdens.

rows.title: CT on pace for another multibillion-dollar budget surplus
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration projects CT will be nearly $2.3 billion in the black this fiscal year but continued to urge caution.

rows.title: Over 154k CT private sector essential workers seek COVID bonuses
rows.standfirst: Soaring demand for the COVID bonuses for essential private-sector workers could cut them from a promoted $1,000 to $200 or less.

rows.title: Save or spend? CT legislators could upend budget rules in 2023
rows.standfirst: CT has saved $9 billion since 2017, but some say the budget constraints need to be loosened as pressures hit families and workers.

rows.title: CT leaders mull special session for essential worker relief, gas tax
rows.standfirst: Connecticut lawmakers may call a special session after elections to extend the gas tax holiday and add money to the Premium Pay Program.
